certifications.name: Fairtrade
certifications.meaning: Farmers and workers receive fair prices and work under safer, fairer conditions.

certifications.name: FSC (Forest Stewardship Council)
certifications.meaning: Wood and paper come from responsibly managed forests.

certifications.name: GOTS (Global Organic Textile Standard)
certifications.meaning: Textiles made from organic fibres, processed under environmental and social rules.

certifications.name: Energy Star
certifications.meaning: Appliances and electronics meet strict energy-efficiency requirements.

certifications.name: EU Energy Label
certifications.meaning: Appliances are rated A to G for energy efficiency, A being the most efficient.
certifications.whereSeen: Washing machines, fridges, TVs sold in the EU.

certifications.name: USDA Organic
certifications.meaning: Food grown without most synthetic pesticides and fertilisers, under US organic rules.
certifications.whereSeen: Packaged food, produce, dairy in the US.

certifications.name: EU Organic Leaf
certifications.meaning: Food produced under the European Union's organic farming rules.
certifications.whereSeen: Food and drink sold in the EU.

certifications.name: Rainforest Alliance
certifications.meaning: Farms and forests are audited against sustainability standards for people and nature.

certifications.name: Certified B Corporation
certifications.meaning: The whole company meets verified standards of social and environmental performance.
certifications.whereSeen: Company websites, packaging across many industries.

certifications.name: OEKO-TEX Standard 100
certifications.meaning: The textile has been tested and found free of harmful levels of listed substances.

certifications.name: MSC (Marine Stewardship Council)
certifications.meaning: The seafood comes from a fishery certified as sustainably managed.

certifications.name: Leaping Bunny
certifications.meaning: The product and its ingredients were not tested on animals.

guide.title: Look for third-party certification
guide.text: A label from an independent body (like the ones in this directory) means more than a logo the brand designed itself.

guide.title: Specific claims beat vague words
guide.text: "Made with 70% recycled cotton" can be checked; "eco-friendly" and "natural" on their own cannot.

guide.title: Judge the whole company, not one green product
guide.text: One recycled line does not make a brand sustainable if the rest of its range and policies are unchanged.

guide.title: Look for published policies and reports
guide.text: Brands that measure their impact publish numbers and targets you can read; silence is also an answer.
